question:
A 60-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of blood in his urine, lower abdominal pain, and a burning sensation while micturating. Five months ago, he was diagnosed with high-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma and a deep vein thrombosis of his right popliteal vein. His medications include polychemotherapy every 3 weeks and a daily subcutaneous dose of low molecular weight heparin. The last cycle of chemotherapy was 2 weeks ago. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 94/min, and blood pressure is 110/76 mm Hg. Examination shows bilateral axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and mild suprapubic tenderness. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL
Leukocytes 4,300/mm3
Platelet count 145,000/mm3
Partial thromboplastin time 55 seconds
Prothrombin time 11 seconds (INR=1)
Urine
RBCs 50–55/hpf
RBC casts negative
WBCs 7/hpf
Epithelial cells 5/hpf
Bacteria occasional
Administration of which of the following is most likely to have prevented this patient's current condition?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Low molecular weight heparin -> anticoagulant effect -> reduced risk of thrombosis -> 80% CHAIN: Chemotherapy -> immunosuppression -> increased susceptibility to infections -> 70% CHAIN: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma -> lymphadenopathy -> increased risk of urinary tract infections -> 60% CHAIN: Deep vein thrombosis -> venous stasis -> predisposition to urinary tract infections -> 80%
enhanced_information: The administration of low molecular weight heparin is most likely to have prevented this patient's current condition. This is supported by the fact that anticoagulants like heparin reduce the risk of thrombosis, which is crucial in a patient with a history of deep vein thrombosis and undergoing chemotherapy for high-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The evidence paths confirm the relationship between deep vein thrombosis and venous stasis, which predisposes to urinary tract infections.
analysis: The core medical principle here is the prevention of thrombosis in a patient with a history of deep vein thrombosis and undergoing chemotherapy. Low molecular weight heparin is a standard anticoagulant used to prevent thrombosis in such patients. The enhanced information provided further supports the use of heparin in this context.
